title: Memory Arena and Pool Library
hints: Aligning the pointer: `std::size_t offset{ (m_used + alignment - 1) / alignment * alignment };` rounds `m_used` up to a multiple of `alignment` (lesson 13.02).

An arena never frees one object; `reset()` throws everything away at once. Objects with destructors that matter must be destroyed by hand first (`p->~T()`), which is why arenas suit plain data like particles.
requirements: An `Arena` that hands out memory from one big buffer by moving a pointer forward (a bump allocator), with `allocate(size, alignment)`, `reset()` and a `used()` count
`create<T>(args...)` that builds an object in the arena with placement `new`
A `Pool<T>` of fixed-size slots with a free list: `acquire()` and `release(T*)`
A short test of each, and a timing against `new` and `delete` for 100,000 small objects
stretch: Expose the arena as a `std::pmr::memory_resource` and use it with `std::pmr::vector`.
